name: Itraconazole
route_note: oral capsules with food or oral solution on an empty stomach, once or twice daily; IV form discontinued in many countries

discovery.note: Lipophilic triazole developed from ketoconazole with broader spectrum, including Aspergillus and dimorphic fungi.

tagline: Broad-spectrum triazole for histoplasmosis, nail fungus and chronic aspergillosis
summary: Itraconazole is a broad-spectrum triazole active against yeasts, dermatophytes, Aspergillus and the endemic dimorphic fungi. It is a first-line treatment for histoplasmosis, blastomycosis, sporotrichosis and chronic pulmonary aspergillosis and is also used for fungal nail infections. Its absorption is variable and it interacts with many drugs through strong CYP3A4 inhibition.
mechanism: Azoles inhibit lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51, encoded by ERG11 in yeasts and cyp51A in Aspergillus), a fungal cytochrome P450 enzyme needed to make ergosterol, the main sterol of fungal cell membranes. Ergosterol depletion and accumulation of toxic 14α-methylated sterols disrupt membrane structure and the function of membrane-bound enzymes, stopping fungal growth.

Itraconazole is highly lipophilic and concentrates in skin, nails and fatty tissues, which suits it to dermatophyte and nail infections. Its poor and variable absorption led to formulations with cyclodextrin (oral solution) and 'super-bioavailable' (SUBA) capsules.
uses: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis and allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (adjunct)
Talaromycosis (penicilliosis) treatment and prophylaxis in HIV

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Itraconazole is synthesised at Janssen in Belgium.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Sporanox capsules are approved in the US.

history.title: Heart failure warning
history.detail: The FDA adds a boxed warning on congestive heart failure after reports in patients treated for onychomycosis.

history.title: WHO essential medicine
history.detail: Itraconazole is added to the WHO Model List, notably for histoplasmosis and chronic pulmonary aspergillosis.

history.title: SUBA formulation
history.detail: Tolsura (SUBA-itraconazole) is approved in the US for systemic fungal infections.

pk.bioavailability: about 55% with food (capsules); higher and more consistent with solution or SUBA
pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP3A4 to hydroxy-itraconazole (active); strong CYP3A4 inhibitor

safety.boxed_warning: Congestive heart failure (do not use for onychomycosis in patients with ventricular dysfunction) and serious drug interactions with CYP3A4 substrates that can cause QT prolongation and fatal arrhythmias (US label).

facts: Capsules need stomach acid and food for absorption, while the oral solution is better absorbed fasting.
Itraconazole remains in nails for months after a course ends, allowing 'pulse' dosing for onychomycosis.
